messages:
jen (support): Customer reported SSE stream that starts then stops with partial output. They see status 200, a few events, then the connection closes; client then reconnects and resumes a new stream. Billing shows tokens for partial output charged, customer upset. Repro steps below.

maria (customer-success): customer says it happens ~1-2x/day, mostly behind corporate proxies. Reproduced with Chrome and a Node fetch wrapper.

jen (support): repro they used: 
```bash
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' \"https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-alpha\"
```
They also sent a small log: 
```
[2026-03-12T14:06:12Z] conn_open id=abc123 remote=198.51.100.22
[2026-03-12T14:06:20Z] send: event:data chunk=...
[2026-03-12T14:06:22Z] write error: broken pipe
[2026-03-12T14:06:22Z] conn_close id=abc123 errno=EPIPE
```

alex (eng-runtime): thanks, dumping quick theory: client or intermediate proxy is silently dropping idle streaming connections (half-closed). Server write hits EPIPE once kernel buffer gone. We currently only send periodic data when model outputs tokens; if there's long prefix or think-time no bytes are written and intermediaries can idle-timeout.

ryan (eng-sre): ALB/NGINX/proxy idle timeouts are usual suspects. What proxy in front of this customer? Any X-Forwarded info?

maria (customer-success): customer uses a corporate proxy + an internal F5. They confirmed ALB idle_timeout is default 60s on their side.

alex (eng-runtime): quick mitigation options:
- emit SSE comment pings (":

") every 15s at the edge (low overhead)
- enable TCP keepalive on server sockets with faster intervals for dedicated/private deployments
- improve detection: track last_write_ts and last_read_ts per connection and proactively close and reprovision if dead for >2x expected interval

jen (support): customer asked if we can do something now on hosted side, they don't want to run in Dedicated.

alex (eng-runtime): we can enable comment pings in the streaming handler behind a feature flag today. Impl notes: send ": noop

" as an SSE comment (not an event) to avoid affecting parsers. Some clients (fetch EventSource) treat comments as keepalive fine. For clients that don't: add "event: noop
 data: 

" fallback. Need testing with browser fetch and node sse parsers.

ryan (eng-sre): also check upstream proxies drop on long-lived TCP with no bytes. For ALB we can advise increasing idle_timeout to 300s for customers under heavy long-pause workloads. For nginx proxies, set proxy_read_timeout and proxy_send_timeout accordingly.

maria (customer-success): customer wants repro steps to validate change. Can we provide curl + Node snippets they can run?

alex (eng-runtime): sure, paste quick Node repro: 
```js
// minimal SSE client (node)
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/streams?model=redwood-alpha', {headers:{Authorization:'Bearer '+process.env.KEY}});
  res.body.on('data', chunk=>console.log('chunk', chunk.toString()));
  res.body.on('end', ()=>console.log('ended'));
})();
```
Then cause pause by sending a prompt that triggers a ~40s think time; observe whether you get comments or sudden close.

jen (support): note about billing: customer is charged for tokens already emitted. They asked if we can avoid charging for partial streams if we detect server-side close due to proxy. What's the policy?

alex (eng-runtime): policy-wise we bill on tokens produced by model output. If connection drops before client ack, tokens still generated. Short-term we can offer a goodwill credit case-by-case but long-term product change would be to buffer and only commit billing after final delivery confirmation — that's a much larger design (and has other abuse vectors).

ryan (eng-sre): operational telemetry suggestions: add metric connection_last_write_seconds and a tag for close_reason (EPIPE, timeout, client-reset). Dashboards to show spikes in EPIPE closes correlated with client IP/prefix and proxy headers. That will help triage corp-proxy clusters.

alex (eng-runtime): implementation plan:
1) rollout comment ping at edge behind flag (15s).
2) add a server-side noop event variant for clients that strip comments.
3) instrument last_write/close_reason logs + dashboard.
4) docs: streaming best-practices + recommended proxy config (ALB idle_timeout >= 300s, nginx proxy_read_timeout >= 300s).

maria (customer-success): customer is ok with temporary workaround if we enable comment pings and share recommended proxy tweaks. Asking for ETA.

alex (eng-runtime): can do flag + rollout to canary tomorrow afternoon, full rollout next week if no regressions. Need a quick regression matrix: browsers (Chrome/Firefox), node EventSource libs, curl.

deploy-bot: deployment started: canary/stream-keepalive-pings -> env=canary (sha:abcde) :rocket:

jen (support): I'll tell the customer we have a canary starting and provide repro snippets + proxy config recommendations. Will also open a billing ticket for potential credit review. :thumbsup:

maria (customer-success): thanks everyone, will follow up with customer after canary completes. :eyes:
